title: Associated primes after a flat base change (Bourbaki)
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $M$ an $R$-module and $N$ an $S$-module which is flat as an $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For a ring $T$ and a $T$-module $P$ call a prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset T$ an associated prime of $P$ if $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_T(z)=\{a\in T:az=0\}$ for some $z\in P$, and write $\operatorname{Ass}_T(P)$ for the set of them. Then $$\operatorname{Ass}_S(M\otimes_RN)\supseteq\bigcup_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(M)}\operatorname{Ass}_S(N/\mathfrak pN),$$ where $M\otimes_RN$ is an $S$-module through $N$; and if $R$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], equality holds.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), lines 15774-15851 (statement 15774-15783, proof 15785-15851); tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags: 0312,algebra-lemma-bourbaki

proof.text: For p = Ann_R(z), form the injective R-linear map R/p → M by r̄ ↦ rz. Tensor on the left with the flat module N. Prove that restriction of scalars carries the S-submodule (p : Set R) • ⊤ to p • ⊤ as an R-submodule, by scalar-product induction. TensorProduct.tensorQuotEquivQuotSMul then constructs an S-linear equivalence N/pN ≃ N ⊗_R (R/p): its S-linearity is checked on quotient representatives. Compose with the tensor injection. Injective S-linear maps preserve the exact element annihilator, so Ass_S(N/pN) is contained in Ass_S(N ⊗_R M).

source.place: Tag 0312, first proof paragraph; quotient/scalar compatibility written out by U1

proof.text: Every element of M ⊗_R N comes from L ⊗_R N for some finitely generated R-submodule L of M (Submodule.exists_fg_le_eq_rTensor_subtype). The subtype tensor map is injective by flatness. Therefore the element has the same annihilator in L ⊗_R N. Apply this argument both to associated_flat_tensor (over R) and to associated_tensor_prime_quotient (over S, after tensor commutation). This implements the directed-union reduction witness by witness, without a separate union theorem.

Over Noetherian R, first prove: if p ∈ Ass_R(M ⊗_R N), then p ∈ Ass_R(M). For finite M put A = R_p and L = M_p. The tensor localization map g : M ⊗_R N → L ⊗_R N is an IsLocalizedModule by the rTensor instance. Mathlib Module.associatedPrimes.mem_associatedPrimes_of_comap_mem_associatedPrimes_of_isLocalizedModule puts the maximal ideal of A among associated primes of L ⊗_R N. This is the Noetherian specialization of associated-prime localization, using isAssociatedPrime_iff to remove radicals. If that maximal ideal were not associated to L, choose x in it acting injectively on L. Flatness of N preserves the injectivity of the R-linear map given by x, hence x acts injectively on L ⊗_R N. But the associated-prime witness is nonzero and killed by x, a contradiction. Descend association of the maximal ideal from L to M by the finitely-generated-comap localization lemma. A is Noetherian and L is finite by the localization instances.

source.place: Tag 0312, contraction paragraph; the equivalent argument localizing only over R is written by U1

proof.text: Given q ∈ Ass_S(N ⊗_R M), restrict its annihilator witness to R: the exact annihilator becomes q.comap (algebraMap R S), and this ideal is prime. R is Noetherian, so isAssociatedPrime_iff turns this witness into Mathlib association over R. Commute tensor factors and apply the preceding R-linear contraction result, then convert back to the exact-annihilator notion. The finite-submodule reduction in step 2 makes this valid for arbitrary M.

source.place: Tag 0312, contraction paragraph; scalar restriction variant written by U1

proof.text: For finite M, apply IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime, the induction principle derived from the prime filtration. In the subsingleton case the tensor has no exact associated prime because Ann(0) is the improper ideal. In the prime-quotient case tensor the supplied equivalence. For a short exact sequence tensor its maps with N: flatness gives injectivity and exactness, and right exactness gives surjectivity. Apply annihilatorAssociatedPrimes_of_shortExact over S and use the induction hypothesis in each outer module. This yields a prime p of R such that q ∈ Ass_S(N ⊗_R (R/p)). The finite-submodule reduction of step 2 removes the finiteness restriction.

source.place: Tag 0312, last proof paragraph, using the prime-filtration induction principle

proof.text: If p is prime and q ∈ Ass_R(R/p), then q = p. Its annihilator witness is nonzero since q is proper. Write it as r̄ with r ∉ p; a kills r̄ exactly when ar ∈ p, which by primality is equivalent to a ∈ p. Now contract both the original q ∈ Ass_S(N ⊗_R M) and its occurrence in N ⊗_R (R/p) from step 5. Step 4 and this quotient calculation identify p with q ∩ R and show p ∈ Ass_R(M). Transfer q across the S-linear quotient/tensor equivalence to Ass_S(N/pN). This proves the reverse inclusion for Noetherian R. Combine with step 1 and transport the two sets along the S-linear tensor-commutation equivalence to the module action in the original statement.

proof_origin.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), proof; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0312. The contraction argument localizes only over R; the finite-submodule reduction is elementwise and the filtration is Mathlib induction.
